holisticNarrative.summary:
The primary evidence is unusually concise: one short PDF with six category statements and no structural details. That document does establish meaningful baseline intent by naming major clinical categories (demographics, medications/allergies, problems, labs, encounter summaries, and chart documents) and by declaring concrete output modalities (Excel, PDF, CDA, and document references). This is more than a bare certification placeholder, but not enough to support confident interoperability engineering.

The practical limitation is not access but semantics. There are no field definitions, join keys, constraints, value sets, or samples. Under the designated-record-set EHI lens, this prevents a defensible determination that all patient-decision and billing/payment records are represented, especially for a product described as an integrated EHR plus practice-management platform. For migration work, this export path would require substantial reverse engineering before quality and completeness could be trusted.
